Posterior edge probabilities for every group and pair of groups

Source: R/edge_probs.R
edge_probs.Rd

Returns per-edge posterior summaries computed from running sums that every sampler keeps over all post-burn-in iterations, so they are available without saving draws (save_draws = FALSE). Each probability is counted per MCMC iteration and then averaged, never assembled from the groups' marginal summaries: the groups are dependent through the MRF prior (G-Wishart, SSVS) or the correlation of edge scales (mGHS).

Usage

edge_probs(fit, scale = c("precision", "pcor"), c = NULL, chain = NULL)

Arguments

fit

A multiggm_fit or multiggm_fit_list.

scale

"precision" (default) or "pcor": the scale of mean, sd, p_exceed_*, p_union_* and p_sign.

c

Thresholds for the magnitude and union probabilities. NULL (default) uses the grid given by diff_deltas at fit time. Values outside that grid are computed from saved draws when the fit has them (for mGHS this also needs the shrinkage-weight draws), and are an error otherwise.

chain

NULL (default) pools all chains; an integer selects chains.

Value

A data frame with columns type, group1, group2, i, j and the quantities above. Edges are in R's upper.tri() order. Attributes: scale, c, n_draws, method and, for mGHS, t_hat.

Details

Rows with type = "group" describe group group1; rows with type = "pair" describe the difference \(D = x_{group1} - x_{group2}\) for every pair of groups. Columns:

mean, sd

Posterior mean and SD of the precision entry or partial correlation (group rows) or of \(D\) (pair rows).

p_struct

Structural probability. Group rows: the edge's posterior inclusion probability \(P(G_{k,ij} = 1)\) for G-Wishart and SSVS; for mGHS \(P(w_{k,ij} > 0.5)\), where \(w = \lambda^2 / (1 + \lambda^2)\) is the shrinkage weight (the paper's \(\kappa\)). Pair rows: \(P(G_s \ne G_t)\), or for mGHS \(P(S_s \ne S_t)\) with \(S = 1(w > 0.5)\).

mean_weight

mGHS group rows: \(E[w]\). The authors' median-probability rule selects \(E[w] > 0.5\) (Busatto & Stingo, Section 5).

p_cut

mGHS: probability of the cut-model indicator, \(P(Z = 1)\) (group rows) or \(P(Z_s \ne Z_t)\) (pair rows).

p_exceed_<c>

\(P(|x| > c)\) (group rows) or \(P(|D| > c)\) (pair rows).

p_union_<c>

Pair rows: \(P(\textrm{structural difference or } |D| > c)\), counted per iteration. The structural part is the edge indicator for G-Wishart and SSVS and the cut-model indicator for mGHS.

p_sign

\(\max\{P(x > 0), P(x < 0)\}\) (group rows) or \(\max\{P(D > 0), P(D < 0)\}\) (pair rows). A central credible interval at level \(L\) excludes zero exactly when p_sign \(> (1 + L) / 2\); the graphical horseshoe's published rule (Li, Craig & Bhadra 2019) is \(L = 0.5\), i.e. p_sign > 0.75 (select_edges(rule = "interval")). For pairs it is not a probability that the edge differs (see diff_summary()).

mean_shrinkage, p_shrinkage, mcse_shrinkage

mGHS group rows: \(E[1 - \kappa]\), \(P(1 - \kappa > 0.5)\) and the Monte Carlo SE of the latter, where \(\kappa\) is the edge's shrinkage factor with the global scale included (see select_edges(), rule = "shrinkage").

p_up_<c>, p_down_<c>

Pair rows: \(P(D > c)\) and \(P(D < -c)\), the direction of a difference: with \(D = x_{group1} - x_{group2}\), p_up means the entry is larger in group1. They add up to p_exceed_<c>.

mcse_struct, mcse_cut, mcse_exceed_<c>, mcse_union_<c>

Batch-means Monte Carlo standard errors of p_struct, p_cut, p_exceed_<c> and p_union_<c> (NA if the fit was made with mcse_batches = 0 or by an older version). With several chains they are pooled as for the probabilities. An edge whose probability is within about two Monte Carlo SEs of a selection cutoff needs a longer run.

Columns that do not apply are NA.

mGHS structural and cut-model probabilities are weak. Following the paper, \(w = \lambda^2 / (1 + \lambda^2)\) uses the local scale only. The horseshoe shrinks null edges mainly through the global scale \(\tau\), so for a null edge \(\lambda\) stays close to its half-Cauchy prior, under which \(P(w > 0.5) = 0.5\). Hence p_struct and mean_weight are near 0.5 for null edges, and \(P(S_s \ne S_t)\) is near 0.5 for edges that are null in both groups. The cut-model indicator is drawn as \(Z \sim \textrm{Bernoulli}(\Phi(w - t))\) (the upstream code; the paper uses the closed-form \(P(w > t \mid \cdot)\)), so \(P(Z = 1)\) lies in about (0.16, 0.84) and \(P(Z_s \ne Z_t)\) is near 0.5 for most edges. For differential edges with mGHS, use the magnitude rule. The authors select edges by \(E[w] > 0.5\) (rule = "median_shrinkage") or by \(E[w] > \hat t_k\), with \(\hat t_k\) the posterior mean threshold (attribute t_hat).

For mGHS the result also carries the posterior mean cut-model threshold per group as attribute t_hat, for the authors' rule \(E[w] > \hat t_k\).

See also

edge_prob_matrix(), select_edges(), select_diff_edges()

Examples

sim <- simulate_multiggm(K = 2, p = 6, n = 60, seed = 1)
fit <- multiggm_mcmc(data_list = sim$data_list, method = "ssvs",
                     burnin = 100, nsave = 100, save_draws = FALSE)
ep <- edge_probs(fit)
head(ep[ep$type == "pair", ])
